notice: RN bank batch 127: Trauma and environmental case studies: splenic injury, heat stroke, hypothermia and mass-casualty triage, with four standalone items. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: A pedestrian struck by a car is in the trauma bay. Using the trauma note, fill in the bowtie: the likely cause of the shock in the middle, two priority interventions on the left and two parameters that show the response on the right.

condition.text: Hemorrhage from an unstable pelvic fracture

actions.text: Rock the pelvis again to confirm that it is unstable
Insert a urinary catheter at once to measure output
Give a large volume of crystalloid first

rationale.correct: An unstable pelvis with shock needs a binder and blood products.

perOption.c2: Heart rate is fast, not slow.
perOption.c3: Too early, and no hypoxemia or petechiae.
perOption.c4: No distended neck veins or muffled heart sounds.
perOption.a4: Blood at the meatus suggests a urethral injury.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize and act on pelvic fracture hemorrhage.

exhibits.title: Trauma bay
exhibits.body: Pedestrian struck by a car. BP 78/44 mm Hg, HR 136/min. The pelvis moved on gentle compression. Blood at the urinary meatus. Alert, pupils equal.

questions.stem: A client has a new long-leg cast after a tibia fracture. For each trend, choose the interpretation.

cells.text: Pink, pink, pale, pale and cool
Normal, normal, tingling, numb between the first and second toes

options.text: Rising pain out of proportion; report now
Expected after a fracture
Needs a stronger opioid only
Worsening perfusion
Normal variation
Improving
Nerve compression
From the opioid
Normal after casting

rationale.correct: Rising pain, pallor and numbness under a cast mean compartment syndrome; the cast may need bivalving.

perOption.b3:b: Opioids do not cause focal numbness.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse receives handoff on four orthopedic trauma clients at 0700. After handoff, which client should the nurse assess first?

options.text: A client 1 day after a total knee replacement who rates pain 6 out of 10 and wants the next dose of oxycodone
A client 2 days after a femur fracture who is newly confused with an SpO2 of 88%
A client in a cast who reports itching under the cast and asks for a coat hanger
A client after hip surgery whose drain has 150 mL of blood since the last shift

rationale.correct: New confusion with hypoxemia after a long-bone fracture is the priority.

perOption.a: Needs pain relief soon, but is stable.
perOption.b: Possible fat embolism; hypoxemia is the most urgent.
perOption.d: Within expected limits; check after the hypoxic client.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: On an infectious disease unit, which tasks can the RN delegate to the UAP? Select all that apply.

options.text: Take vital signs on a client in contact precautions for MRSA
Restock gowns and gloves outside isolation rooms
Bathe a client with C. difficile using soap and water for hand hygiene afterward
Assess a client with HIV for new oral lesions
Teach a client with TB how to take the medicines at home
Decide when a client's airborne precautions can stop

rationale.correct: UAPs do routine care with correct precautions; assessment, teaching and decisions stay with the RN.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

rationale.correct: Shock with free fluid after blunt trauma means internal bleeding.

perOption.r1: Hypotension; class III or IV hemorrhage.

rows.text: Heart rate 138/min with falling blood pressure
Normal blood pressure with heart rate 105 and anxiety
Confusion and very low urine output
Narrowed pulse pressure with normal systolic pressure

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The priority is {{b1}} with {{b2}}, while preparing for {{b3}}.

options.text: damage-control resuscitation
aggressive crystalloid boluses to a normal blood pressure
a CT scan before any treatment
observation
balanced blood products (plasma, platelets and red cells) and tranexamic acid
albumin only
vitamin K
dextrose 50%
emergency laparotomy or splenic embolization
discharge
an outpatient ultrasound
physiotherapy

rationale.correct: Balanced products, TXA and source control.

perOption.b1:c: Unstable clients do not go to CT.

questions.stem: The massive transfusion protocol is activated. Which actions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use a blood warmer
Check ionized calcium
Give tranexamic acid within 3 hours of injury
Monitor potassium
Give products cold straight from the fridge to save time
Wait for the full crossmatch before any blood

rationale.correct: Warm products, replace calcium, give TXA and monitor potassium.

perOption.f: Uncrossmatched O blood is used in emergencies.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

exhibits.title: MTP
exhibits.body: Uncrossmatched O negative red cells, plasma and platelets 1:1:1. TXA 1 g IV.

questions.stem: After 8 units, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Warm the client with a forced-air blanket
Give calcium as prescribed
Report the results to the trauma team
Stop all blood products because of the acidosis
Give sodium bicarbonate to correct the pH as the main fix

rationale.correct: Hypothermia, acidosis and coagulopathy form the lethal triad.

perOption.e: Treat the cause: perfusion and bleeding.

questions.stem: After a splenectomy, for each statement or finding at discharge, indicate whether it shows understanding or progress, or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Hemoglobin stable at 9.8 g/dL for 48 hours
"I'll get the pneumococcal, meningococcal and Hib vaccines."
"A fever is no big deal now, I can wait a few days."
"I'll wear a medical alert bracelet."
Platelets 820,000/mm3 on day 5

rationale.correct: After splenectomy, vaccines and urgent care for fever are essential.

perOption.r3:c1: Overwhelming infection risk; seek care at once.
perOption.r3:c2: Overwhelming infection risk; seek care at once.
perOption.r5:c1: Reactive thrombocytosis; clot risk is reviewed.
perOption.r5:c2: Reactive thrombocytosis; clot risk is reviewed.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
CDC/ACIP immunization schedules

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that define heat stroke.

rationale.correct: A core temperature above 40 C with altered mental status is heat stroke.

perOption.r3: Sweating is common in exertional heat stroke and does not rule it out.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it fits heat exhaustion or heat stroke.

rows.text: Temperature 39 C with normal mental status
Confusion or seizures
Heavy sweating, nausea and headache with a clear mind
Temperature above 40 C with combative behavior

rationale.correct: Mental status separates heat stroke from heat exhaustion.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

options.text: cooling to below 39 C within 30 minutes
transport first and cool at the hospital
antipyretics
oral fluids only
cold-water immersion
a fan alone
a warm shower
acetaminophen

rationale.correct: Cool first with cold-water immersion.

perOption.b1:a: Time at high temperature determines organ damage.
perOption.b1:c: Do not work in heat stroke.
perOption.b1:d: Not enough and unsafe if confused.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which actions should the nurse include during cooling? Select all that apply.

options.text: Monitor rectal temperature continuously
Remove from the water at about 38.6 to 39 C
Protect the airway and watch for seizures
Give acetaminophen to bring the temperature down
Cool until the temperature reaches 35 C

rationale.correct: Continuous core temperature, stop at 39 C and protect the airway.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Cooling
exhibits.body: Placed in an ice-water tub. Rectal probe in place.

questions.stem: At the hospital 6 hours later, review the results. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Report the CK and creatinine
Expect IV fluids to keep urine output up
Monitor for bleeding
Check liver enzymes again
Discharge home now that the temperature is normal
Restart the stimulant at the usual dose tonight

rationale.correct: Heat stroke injures muscle, kidneys, liver and clotting.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Laboratory reference ranges as used in common NCLEX review texts; follow the facility's ranges

questions.educationalObjective: Take action on heat stroke complications.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll return to running gradually after my doctor clears me."
"I'll acclimatize to the heat over 1 to 2 weeks before races."
"I'll talk to my prescriber about the stimulant before races."
"If I feel confused while running, I'll push through to finish."
"I'll run at midday because it's when I have time."

rationale.correct: Acclimatize, return gradually, review medicines and avoid the hottest hours.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that show moderate to severe hypothermia.

rationale.correct: No shivering, bradycardia and J waves at 29 C mean moderate hypothermia.

questions.stem: For each statement, indicate whether it is accurate or inaccurate about the hypothermic heart.

rows.text: Rough handling can trigger ventricular fibrillation
Defibrillation and drugs may not work below 30 C
A client is not dead until warm and dead
Bradycardia should be treated first with atropine
Placing the client upright quickly helps the circulation

rationale.correct: Handle gently, keep horizontal and rewarm.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: This client needs {{b1}}, and the nurse should expect {{b2}} as rewarming proceeds.

options.text: active internal rewarming such as warmed IV fluids and warmed humidified oxygen
only a blanket
a hot bath
rubbing the limbs
hypotension as vessels dilate (rewarming shock)
rising heart rate requiring beta blockers
permanent bradycardia
hypertension

rationale.correct: Active internal rewarming with fluids ready for rewarming shock.

perOption.b1:b: Passive rewarming is for mild cases.
perOption.b1:d: Harms tissue and can cause VF.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Remove wet clothing gently
Warmed IV 0.9% sodium chloride at 40 to 42 C
Forced-air warming blanket to the trunk
Treat the low glucose
Warm the arms and legs first
Move the client briskly onto a stretcher

rationale.correct: Gentle handling, trunk warming and warmed fluids.

perOption.e: Returns cold, acidic blood to the core.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Warm fluids, forced-air blanket, warmed oxygen. Consider extracorporeal rewarming if arrest occurs.

questions.stem: During transfer, the client becomes pulseless and the monitor shows ventricular fibrillation. The core temperature is 29.6 C. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Start high-quality CPR
Defibrillate once as per protocol
Continue active rewarming during CPR
Stop resuscitation after 10 minutes because the client is cold
Give repeated epinephrine every 3 minutes as at normal temperature

rationale.correct: CPR, one shock and continued rewarming; drugs are limited until warmer.

perOption.d: Not dead until warm and dead.
perOption.e: Drugs are held or spaced until warmer.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care

content.template: In a mass-casualty event, the goal of triage changes to {{b1}}, so a client in cardiac arrest is {{b2}}.

questions.stem: To make beds available, the charge nurse reviews inpatients for early discharge. Which clients are appropriate to discharge or transfer? Select all that apply.

options.text: Day 3 of oral antibiotics for cellulitis, afebrile
Knee arthroscopy this morning, walking and eating
Stable COPD, waiting for home oxygen
A client 6 hours after an anterior myocardial infarction with chest pain resolved
A client with DKA whose insulin infusion is being titrated hourly

rationale.correct: Discharge stable clients to create surge capacity.

questions.stem: A family member arrives demanding to see a relative and a news reporter asks the nurse about the injured. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Refer the reporter to the public information officer
Send the family to the family assistance area
Follow the incident command structure
Give the reporter the names of the injured who have been admitted
Let the family member into the treatment area to search for the relative

rationale.correct: Use the incident command roles for media and family.

Client E: radial pulse back after blood, alert
A green client now short of breath with chest pain

rationale.correct: Triage is repeated as clients change.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
